One-sentence judgment: butchers and meat cutters do not just chop up meat and sell it, but cut whole cuts into customer-buyable portions to specification while being responsible for hygiene, weight, labeling, shrinkage, and display. O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (preparation from little to some, SVP below 6.0), does not mark Bright Outlook, and gives interest code RC. The core boundary is: you can cut to order, trim, debone, grind, weigh, label, and display, and you can do receiving inspection and inventory records; but you cannot replace inspection and quarantine or food safety regulatory judgment, you must not keep working when equipment guarding or hygiene conditions are not compliant, and you cannot claim for yourself the decision to stop and restart equipment.

Signals for continued exploration: you can keep your technique steady in cold, damp conditions and long periods of standing; you are willing to cut to the same specification and check weight and labels; you can accept repetitive motion and keep up cleaning and sanitizing; you are willing to stop the machine first and report when you see a problem with knives, saws, or grinding equipment; and you accept a daily work style dominated by counter service, ordering and stocktaking, and handover records.

Conditions for pausing high-cost investment first: you have not yet completed one full closed loop from receiving inspection, cutting specification, weighing and labeling, display, to cleaning and sanitizing and record handover; or you are unwilling to follow hygiene rules and knife safety requirements and only want to go by feel without checking specification and weight; and do not treat having cooked at home as proof that you can independently take a retail cutting station.

Education, qualifications, and authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2 (preparation from little to some, SVP below 6.0), usually requiring a high school diploma or equivalent (GED), with some positions not requiring it, and on-the-job training ranging from a few days to one year. In the United States, position requirements are set by the employer and state rules; in mainland China, food safety and animal epidemic prevention requirements are set by market regulation and agriculture and rural affairs departments stage by stage, positions usually have no unified individual practice license, but positions handling food that goes directly into the mouth may require a health certificate and must follow the hygiene and equipment operating rules of the enterprise (market, supermarket, or processing point). Qualification, health requirements, equipment authorization, and the right to stop work are four different things and cannot substitute for one another.

In one sentence: this is a role that turns whole cuts into sellable portions to specification and is responsible for hygiene, weight, and shrinkage, with outputs of meat cut to specification, weighing and labeling records, display condition, inventory and ordering records, and cleaning, sanitizing, and handover records; it is not an inspection and quarantine regulatory role and does not replace food safety regulatory judgment. Mainland China wage data are not published at occupation level on this page: only the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 rental and business services industry average is used as a prominently labeled explicit proxy, and local real hiring must be checked.

The work of this occupation falls into three categories: first, cutting and processing (cutting to specification, trimming, deboning, tying, and grinding, handling special cuts requested by customers, and controlling yield and shrinkage); second, counter and inventory (weighing, labeling, pricing, display and replenishment, estimating demand, ordering and receiving inspection, and keeping records); third, hygiene and equipment (cleaning and sanitizing meat cases and cutting equipment, checking knife and equipment condition daily, and stopping the machine and reporting through procedure when there is a problem). All three share the same chain centered on hygiene and specification consistency.
Cutting and processing

Confirm the meat and specification requirements → check knife and equipment condition → cut, trim, and debone to specification → handle special cuts requested by customers → control yield and shrinkage → record and complete handover.
Counter and inventory

Weigh, label, and price → display and maintain display condition → replenish as needed → estimate demand and order → receiving inspection and storage as required → keep receiving, issuing, and sales records.

Editorial safety check: for equipment problems, first stop using it under the on-site safety procedure and report, and never bypass guarding. Cleaning, clearing jams, and maintenance covered by US OSHA1910.147 must be isolated, stored energy handled, and verified by trained and authorized personnel under the hazardous energy control procedure; pressing a stop button does not equal isolation. This page does not grant permission to enter a danger zone, perform maintenance, or restart operation, and Chinese positions check applicable rules and equipment procedures separately.

Editorial duty comparison: retail meat cutting differs from chef, food service management, food science, and processing cutting in object and training, and the work may overlap; it is not claimed that chefs never cut, managers never operate, or scientists only write methods.
Core purpose

Give customers safe meat of consistent specification and clear pricing: control quality and shrinkage with standard cutting and hygienic work, keep the transaction clear with accurate weighing and labeling, and maintain sellable condition with display and replenishment.
Main objects and basis

The objects are whole and semi-prepared meat, customer orders and special cut requests, knives, saws, and grinding equipment, display cases and the cold chain, weighing and labeling systems, and inventory and sales records; the basis is cutting specifications and yield standards, food hygiene and cleaning and sanitizing rules, equipment operation and guarding requirements, cold chain temperature and storage requirements, labeling and pricing rules, and the enterprise's handover and reporting procedures.
Core process

Confirm specification and equipment condition, cut and trim to specification, weigh, label, and display, receiving inspection and storage, cleaning, sanitizing, and inspection records, and stopping the machine and reporting on problems with handover.
Main outputs

Retail portion cuts according to specification, special cuts that meet requirements, accurate weighing and labeling, display and replenishment condition, receiving inspection and storage records, ordering and inventory records, cleaning, sanitizing, and equipment inspection records, and handover notes.
Responsible parties

Editorial duty check: confirm with the actual enterprise the division of work and the escalation path for operations, receiving, shift teams, food safety management, and maintenance; this page does not specify the same organizational levels for all enterprises.

Conclusion boundaries

Meat specification and shrinkage records state what the yield looks like under the given specification, equipment condition, and cold chain conditions; they are not a food safety conclusion and do not replace inspection and quarantine judgment or enterprise responsibility, and they are updated as specification, batch, and equipment condition change; the batch and date should be stated when citing them.

Before starting, check at least six items: position duties (leaning toward cutting and processing, counter sales, or receiving and inventory), equipment operation authorization and training arrangements, shift patterns and hours working in a cold environment, protective equipment and knife management rules, health and hygiene requirements (whether a health certificate is needed), and whether ordering and inventory responsibility is included.
Occupation basis

O*NET-SOC51-3021.00 is cutting to retail consumer portions, JobZone1—2/SVP below 6, not marked BrightOutlook. 2025 industry 84% retail, 16% other including manufacturing. O*NET interest RC: R88/C49/E30/S15/A13/I7 are the six type scores; there are also 41 independent specific interest areas, with physical and manual 79, cooking 24, sales 22, and personal service 17, which are not exclusive subcategories of R and are not an individual competence threshold. The one-to-one mapping between the China 2022 occupation classification detailed categories and US 51-3021 was not completed this round and must be checked against actual duties; a publication entry point cannot prove that no corresponding detailed category exists.
Education and training paths

O*NET new entrant education Q&A for this detailed occupation: 70% high school, 20% below high school, 7% some college with no degree, not the incumbent education composition; JobZone1—2/SVP below 6 is the broad preparation level. The typical entry in BLS Table 1.2 is no formal educational credential, related experience None, and moderate-term on-the-job training, which does not mean every employer waives education or experience. In mainland China, Article 44 of the Food Safety Law requires food safety knowledge training for enterprises, and Article 45 requires an annual health examination and a health certificate before working for personnel handling food that goes directly into the mouth, which does not directly extend to all raw meat cutters. Order No. 81 applies to the sale of edible agricultural products in fixed markets and supermarkets, and meat that should be inspected and quarantined by law must be checked with the corresponding certificate obtained and kept; receiving checks do not create government quarantine authority. The US OOH notes that some states or localities require food handler certification, and specific areas are checked separately. This round did not complete the check of Chinese individual licensing and all local requirements and does not claim that there is uniformly no license.

Hiring mentions are not deployment or replacement. Pay and working hours

O*NET93% have a regular schedule; 11% work more than 40 hours per week, 42% exactly 40, and 47% less than 40, so peak overtime is not presumed. The 2025 US exact occupation has a median annual wage of 40140 and an hourly wage of 19.30 US dollars, with P10—P90 annual wages from 29460 to 58110. China NBS2025 wholesale and retail trade urban non-private units pre-tax annual average 135749 yuan and private 69622 yuan (Tables 2 and 5). Retail meat cutting can refer to this industry background, but the statistic mixes wholesale, retail, and multiple occupations and is not the median, starting pay, city monthly salary, or a personal offer for meat cutters and cannot be applied automatically to processing positions. The precise occupational wage remains insufficient evidence. Editorial suggestion: check the real shift, working temperature, protective equipment, training, and the written pay conditions.

Butchers and meat cutters (O*NET-SOC 51-3021.00, Butchers and Meat Cutters) cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments. Daily work includes: cutting meat and arranging products in display cases so they look attractive and draw customers; wrapping, weighing, labeling, and pricing meat; cutting, trimming, deboning, tying, and grinding beef, pork, poultry, and fish to prepare them in cookable form; preparing special cuts requested by customers; receiving, inspecting, and storing meat on arrival to ensure quality; estimating demand and ordering or requisitioning meat supplies to maintain inventory; using boning knives, skewers, and twine to shape, tie, and truss roasts; recording the quantity of meat received and issued or keeping sales records; supervising other butchers or cutters; curing, smoking, tenderizing, and preserving meat; negotiating with supply company representatives to determine order details; and cleaning and sanitizing meat display cases and cutting equipment. It carries responsibility for meat specification, hygienic work, and shrinkage records, but does not replace inspection and quarantine, food safety regulation, or equipment maintenance responsibility. The reference to slaughter in the Chinese name does not expand the duties of US 51-3021 into the 51-3023 slaughtering and meat packing occupation; specific positions are checked separately by retail or processing tasks.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 51-3021.00 Butchers and Meat Cutters, page updated in 2026, listed as Job Zone 1-2 (preparation from little to some, SVP below 6.0), with Bright Outlook not marked. The official duty text is "Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments."; the page lists 12 tasks covering cutting meat and arranging products in display cases to attract customers, wrapping, weighing, labeling, and pricing, cutting, trimming, deboning, tying, and grinding beef, pork, poultry, and fish, preparing special cuts requested by customers, receiving inspection and storage, estimating demand and ordering to maintain inventory, using boning knives, skewers, and twine to shape and truss roasts, recording received and issued quantities or sales, supervising other butchers or cutters, curing, smoking, tenderizing, and preserving, negotiating order details with suppliers, and cleaning and sanitizing meat cases and cutting equipment. The 12 tasks are 7Core, 4Supplemental, and 1 New/NA (cleaning and sanitizing display cases and cutting equipment), not all core tasks; the 41 general work activities, 11 detailed activities, and 57 context items are kept separate.

paragraphs: This page compares butchers and meat cutters with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which direction each preference suits better. Adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions, and this does not mean position titles are interchangeable.

Evidence note: occupational directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 51-3021.00 and the adjacent entries (US basis); hygiene requirements, equipment authorization, and inspection authority must be verified separately for each enterprise and jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares butchers and meat cutters with adjacent directions in duties and outputs; the judgment is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required authorization, not on how similar the position titles are.

Food service managers own store resources and scheduling and are responsible for business results and do not take on the specific cutting technique or yield; this occupation completes cutting, weighing, and hygienic work within the given specification and shift and honestly records shrinkage.

If you would rather be responsible for scheduling, cost, and store operation, look first at the food service manager direction; if you would rather stand at the block and cut meat to specification properly, look first at this occupation.
Be responsible for store operations, scheduling, cost, and compliance, with outputs mainly business metrics, staffing arrangements, and process rules.
Food service managers (Food Service Managers)

What food scientists produce is processes and standard methods, and their work is mainly laboratory and document based; what this occupation produces is sellable portion meat, and the work is mainly at the block and in the cold chain.

If you would rather do formulation, process, and standards research, look first at the food scientist direction; if you would rather do on-site cutting and store delivery, look first at this occupation.
Research and develop formulations, processes, and safety standards, with outputs mainly methods, standards, and experimental conclusions.
Food scientists and technologists (Food Scientists and Technologists)

Chefs and head cooks are responsible for dish design, cooking, and the taste of what is served, and purchasing and cutting are mostly upstream steps; this occupation is responsible for portion specification, labeling, and shrinkage and does not carry dish design or cooking responsibility.

If you would rather design dishes and control the taste of what is served, look first at the chef and head cook direction; if you would rather cut and display meat to specification, look first at this occupation.
Design dishes and organize kitchen output and taste control, with outputs mainly dishes and quality of what is served.
Chefs and head cooks (Chefs and Head Cooks)

First-line supervisors center on supervision and scheduling and are responsible for on-site execution but do not carry cutting work of the same intensity; this occupation is the main on-site operator and also documents hygiene and equipment checks.

If you would rather do scheduling and on-site supervision, look first at the first-line supervisor of food preparation and serving workers direction; if you would rather work with your hands and keep specification consistent, look first at this occupation.
Arrange shifts and supervise on-site operations and hygiene execution, with outputs mainly shift operations and inspection records.
First-line supervisors of food preparation and serving workers (First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers)

Fast food cooks work on standardized production of finished meals and hardly touch fresh cutting or weight labeling; this occupation deals with the cutting specification, hygiene, and cold chain of fresh meat, and its responsibility object is the retail transaction.
If you would rather do standardized meal production, look first at the fast food cook direction; if you would rather handle fresh meat and portion specification, look first at this occupation.
Produce finished meals under standardized processes, with outputs mainly serving speed and standard recipes.
Fast food cooks (Cooks, Fast Food)

Meat, poultry, and fish cutters and trimmers work on processing line batches and complete cutting to standard work, usually not facing customers directly and not carrying retail labeling, display, or pricing; this occupation deals with retail portions and customer requests and is also responsible for display, labeling, and inventory.

If you would rather do batch cutting in a processing environment, look first at the cutter and trimmer direction; if you would rather face customers for retail portions and display, look first at this occupation.
Cut and trim meat in batches in a processing environment, with outputs mainly batch processing volume and standard work.
Meat, poultry, and fish cutters and trimmers (Meat, Poultry, and Fish Cutters and Trimmers)

Conclusion: the choice of direction is based on main outputs, responsibility objects, and required authorization, not on how similar the names are; once a direction is chosen, check item by item the target position's working environment, equipment operation authorization, hygiene and health requirements, and shift and hours working in a cold environment, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

First complete one closed loop with simulated materials: cut to specification and record the yield, complete weighing and labeling, do one round of cleaning and sanitizing and equipment checks, then have a practitioner point out hygiene and safety problems; at the same time check the target position's equipment operation authorization, shift and hours working in a cold environment, and health and hygiene requirements.
Practicing butchers and meat cutters

Use tools for reviewable steps such as order estimation, shift reminders, and drafting labels and records; cutting specification and yield, receiving inspection conclusions, hygiene and equipment condition judgments, and stopping work and reporting on problems must still be checked and documented by the operator.
Store and processing point management positions

Before introducing automatic ordering or electronic labels, first clarify the data sources and update timing, how exceptions are handled, who reviews order quantities against actual shrinkage, and how cleaning and temperature records are kept, so that any automatic result can be checked back against actual inventory and cold chain records, and human responsibility for food safety and hygienic work is retained.
Training and mentoring

Focus training on cutting technique and yield, knife and equipment safety, cleaning, sanitizing, and the cold chain, and weighing, labeling, and record standards; also train the habit of checking electronic records, especially the sources of batch, temperature, and shrinkage figures.

Order estimation, shift reminders, and labels and records are editorial assisted scenarios; this round obtained no AI replacement ratio or effect statistics for this exact occupation. Task exposure, automation, and employment projections are kept separate.

entries.answer: Cut, trim, or prepare consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments: display meat cuts and products in cases, wrap, weigh, label, and price, cut, trim, debone, tie, and grind beef, pork, poultry, and fish, prepare special cuts requested by customers, receive, inspect, and store meat on arrival, estimate demand and order to maintain inventory, record received and issued quantities or sales, supervise other cutters, cure and preserve meat, and clean and sanitize meat cases and cutting equipment.
entries.question: What do butchers and meat cutters do every day?

entries.answer: The main risks are cuts and mechanical injury from knives and equipment, strain from repetitive motion and long standing, injury from cold, damp conditions and slippery floors, food safety risk from a cold chain break or out-of-range temperature, cross-contamination from inadequate cleaning and sanitizing, transaction information mismatch from an uncalibrated scale or a wrong label, and working beyond equipment authorization; controls rely on standard use and checks, protective equipment and stopping work to report, cleaning and temperature records, periodic scale calibration and label checks, and a clear authorization and escalation process.
entries.question: What risks most need attention in advance in this job?

entries.answer: Fit signals are being able to keep your technique steady under cold and repetitive motion, being willing to cut to specification and check weight and labels, and being able to stop the machine first and report when equipment is abnormal; being able to cook or being strong is not enough to prove competence, and what matters is whether there are reviewable cutting output, cleaning, and equipment inspection records.

subject.name: Butchers and meat cutters
subject.summary: The entries on this page correspond to butchers and meat cutters (O*NET-SOC 51-3021.00, Butchers and Meat Cutters): cutting, trimming, or preparing consumer-sized portions of meat for use or sale in retail establishments — cutting, trimming, deboning, tying, and grinding to specification, handling special cuts requested by customers, wrapping, weighing, labeling, and pricing, display and replenishment, estimating demand and ordering, receiving inspection and storage, and cleaning and sanitizing meat cases and cutting equipment and completing handover records; the work is mainly hand work while standing for long periods (86% standing continuously, 93% using hands continuously, 82% exposed to hazardous equipment every day, and 86% wearing protective equipment every day), and its duties do not equal inspection and quarantine or food safety regulation, nor do they replace equipment maintenance or store management decisions.
